configuration: ABot-Claw as described in arXiv:2604.10096v2 (v2, 17 Apr 2026): the OpenClaw runtime orchestrating a heterogeneous fleet (Piper arm, Unitree G1, Unitree Go2) with the shared SpatialMemory service (object / place / keyframe / semantic-frame memory) and the online VLAC progress critic; judged together with the repository at commit 39c9ffc94a84f2e6baac431a9bff9771111f8539 (openclaw_layer workspace files and skills, service_layer SpatialMemory / VLAC / GraspAnything, robot_layer Piper agent server). The G1 and Go2 robot clients and the OpenClaw runtime itself are not in the repository.

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: The paper describes detector output being written into the shared memory (Sec. 2.3) and successful executions being written back (Sec. 2.5). The code implements the write path: SpatialMemory exposes POST /memory/object/upsert, /memory/place/upsert, /memory/semantic/ingest and /memory/keyframe/ingest-batch (app/api/routes.py:28-42), persisting rows to SQLite plus JPEG evidence (app/services/memory_service.py:64-183, app/storage.py:79-102; ObjectMemoryUpsertRequest.source defaults to 'yolo', app/schemas.py:34). The robot code wrapper pre-creates memory = MemorySDK() with upsert_object (code_executor.py:689-701; robot_sdk/memory_sdk.py:116-159), and the abotclaw-memory skill tells the agent to upsert 'after visual detection plus pose estimation' and to 'get camera frame from robot SDK ... call /memory/semantic/ingest or /memory/object/upsert' (SKILL.md:136-149, 222-226).

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: The paper states the runtime queries memory before acting and that memory supplies place anchors and object observations to localize targets (Sec. 2.5), that retrieval returns an action-ready representation with a 3D pose (Sec. 2.3), and in the 4.3.2 demo the runtime queries shared memory for the quadruped's last known location to reassign the task. The code implements the read path: /query/object, /query/place, /query/position, /query/semantic/text and /query/unified return target_pose, confidence and evidence (app/api/routes.py:44-70; memory_service.py:185-278); MemorySDK.query_object is pre-created in the robot wrapper (memory_sdk.py:182-199); the abotclaw-memory skill instructs 'query /query/object; read target_pose; hand off target_pose to navigation or manipulation' (SKILL.md:210-214) and MISSION.md:41 directs memory use when prior observations may help the task.
M->A.locator: Paper Sec. 2.5 'Instruction grounding and embodiment selection' and 'Memory-assisted action generation', Sec. 2.3 (action-ready representation), Sec. 4.3.2; service_layer/SpatialMemory/app/api/routes.py:44-70; openclaw_layer/skills/abotclaw-memory/SKILL.md:210-214, 245-247; openclaw_layer/MISSION.md:41

Paper 4.3.2 (UNVERIFIED, identical in three passes): 'ABot-Claw queries the shared memory to recover the quadruped's last known location'. A->S.label: reported
A->S.rationale: Action-side intent and plans guide sensing targets and expected-effect checks. Sec. 2.5 says the critic evaluates progress 'with respect to the original instruction and current observation'; Sec. 2.4 says local refinement includes 'updating the viewpoint, or repeating a short action sequence'; Sec. 4.2.1 describes search procedures in which the manipulator incrementally expands its observable workspace and refines the target observation; Sec. 4.3.1 verifies the grasp result before navigating. In code, the progress-critic skill has the agent assemble task_description plus reference and current frames and POST them to /critic (SKILL.md:29-52, 75-82), which VLAC main.py consumes (lines 54-59, 122-141), an expected-effect check driven by the action's goal; detection is targeted by the action's chosen object via yolo.segment_3d(object_name) (robot_sdk/yolo_sdk.py:302-364); the robot system guide tells the agent to actively monitor /code/status and execution recordings while its code runs (routes/system_guide.py:270-323).
A->S.locator: Paper Sec. 2.4 'Adaptive correction and strategy switching', Sec. 2.5 'Execution and progress evaluation', Sec. 4.2.1, Sec. 4.3.1; openclaw_layer/skills/abotclaw-progress-critic/SKILL.md:29-52, 75-82; service_layer/VLAC/main.py:54-59, 122-141; robot_layer/arm_piper/agent_server/routes/system_guide.py:270-323
A->S.quote: Paper 2.4 (UNVERIFIED: WebFetch extraction, identical in two passes): 'the system keeps the current strategy and attempts local refinement, such as adjusting a target pose, updating the viewpoint, or repeating a short action sequence.' Paper 4.2.1 (UNVERIFIED): 'The manipulator then incrementally expands its observable workspace until the target is detected, after which the system refines the target observation and executes grasping.' SKILL.md:81-82 (verbatim): '5. Call the critic service with all three inputs in one request.\n6. Interpret the response as supervision for task control.'

M->S.label: reported
M->S.rationale: The deployed progress-critic skill routes retained memory content into the interpretation of current observations: the VLAC reference image 'may come from ... a memory/evidence image from abotclaw-memory', and the agent is told to 'use memory to retrieve a prior successful evidence image as reference_image' and 'use the critic to compare the current scene against remembered success state' (SKILL.md:100-107, 166-172). The memory service persists evidence JPEGs and returns evidence.image_path with every hit (memory_service.py:45-48, 217-221), and the critic accepts a path, URL or base64 image (VLAC main.py:68-83; VLAC README 'one-shot ... in-context capabilities'). The retained image is consumed by the interpreting function (the pair-wise critic that scores the current frame), not by an action decision that merely requests a new observation, so this is M->S rather than M->A->S. Caveats: the paper text itself only supports M->A->S (Sec. 2.5: memory 'helps localize the target and reduce unnecessary search'), the Sec. 2.3 keyframe selection 'according to information density and scene novelty' has only a placeholder implementation (pipelines/offline_keyframe_pipeline.py, task_service._simulate_pipeline), and the flow is a configured skill instruction with no reported use in the Sec. 4 demonstrations.
M->S.locator: openclaw_layer/skills/abotclaw-progress-critic/SKILL.md:100-107, 166-172; service_layer/SpatialMemory/app/services/memory_service.py:45-48, 217-221; service_layer/VLAC/main.py:68-83, 130-141; Paper Sec. 2.5 'Memory-assisted action generation' (M->A->S only), Sec. 2.3 keyframe sentence

SKILL.md:168-172 (verbatim): 'This skill works well with `abotclaw-memory`:

- use memory to retrieve a prior successful evidence image as `reference_image`
- use the critic to compare the current scene against remembered success state

A->M.label: reported
A->M.rationale: The paper states that execution traces are logged with critic scores and fed back to the runtime as structured experience (Sec. 2.4) and that successful executions are written back into memory (Sec. 2.5). The robot-side code keeps per-execution action records for later use by the agent: every submitted script is written to logs/code_executions/<timestamp>_<id>.py and appended to an execution history (code_executor.py:436-441, 553-555, 717-725) and to code_execution.log (lines 376-395); ExecutionRecorder stores camera frames, a 10 Hz state_log.jsonl and metadata.json per execution (execution_recorder.py:109-192) and serves them through /code/history, /code/recordings and /code/recordings/{id} (routes/code_routes.py:325-429); the wrapper's memory.upsert_object lets the agent's action code write its results into the shared memory (code_executor.py:700-701). No repository code writes critic scores or 'structured experience' into any store; that part is described only in the paper.

outcome.label: stated
outcome.rationale: Later evidence about the actions is obtained and retained: the paper logs critic scores together with execution traces (Sec. 2.4) and writes successful executions back into memory (Sec. 2.5). In code, each ExecutionResult retains status (completed/failed/timeout/stopped), exit_code, stdout, stderr, error and stop_reason in the executor history and log (code_executor.py:65-81, 487-523, 553-555, 614-629), and ExecutionRecorder retains the observed camera frames and robot state captured during execution (execution_recorder.py:28-31, 196-244), served with frames matched to the nearest state sample (code_routes.py:335-396).

attribution.label: stated
attribution.rationale: The critic outcome is linked to the current subtask or strategy and used to correct execution: Sec. 2.4 specifies completion, local refinement, or replanning depending on the score for the current subtask, and Sec. 4.2.2 reports that a failed grasp was detected by the monitoring module and triggered replanning with recomputed grasp poses. The progress-critic skill encodes the same immediate check (continue / retry / replan / stop from critic output, SKILL.md:145-154), and the system guide tells the agent to stop execution and verify results from recorded frames (system_guide.py:316-322). This is an immediate check; no durable linkage store is implemented in the repository.

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: No statement that the service itself durably changed model parameters, prompts, skills, reusable rules, code, or harness as a result of outcomes. The title and Fig. 2 call the agents 'self-evolving' and Sec. 1 says OpenClaw 'supports natural language–driven dynamic skill evolution', but that describes the base runtime's generic capability, not a reported revision in ABot-Claw. Sec. 2.4's 'structured experience' fed back to the runtime is content consumed by a fixed mechanism, and Sec. 3.2's per-task 'fully executable Python script' is task execution, not a reusable rule; generated scripts are only saved as logs (code_executor.py:717-725) and never reloaded as skills. MISSION.md:51-58 and HEARTBEAT.md:16-25 ask the agent to author reusable skills at user request, with no reported instance. The VLAC critic is inference-only with fixed weights (service_layer/VLAC/main.py:88-99), SpatialMemory stores observations only, and setup.sh copies static skill files. Grep of the repository for critic/experience/learn/fine-tune/retrain in robot_layer and SpatialMemory returns nothing.

later_use.label: not_stated
later_use.rationale: Because no revision is reported, no later step is reported to have run under a revised mechanism. The only forward-looking statement, Sec. 2.4's 'Over time, this creates a closed loop from execution to evaluation and from evaluation to future decision-making', gives no run. The code loads nothing learned or revised: VLAC weights come from a fixed VLAC_MODEL_PATH (main.py:29, 92), skills are static files copied by setup.sh:56-67, and the executor's history is capped at 10 entries and 50 saved scripts without any reload path (code_executor.py:553-555, 645-656).

notes: Judged the single ABot-Claw configuration (OpenClaw orchestration + shared SpatialMemory + online VLAC critic) from the v2 paper and the repository at 39c9ffc. Paper text was obtained through WebFetch extraction because raw download was unavailable in this session; paper quotes are therefore labeled UNVERIFIED, with a note where the same wording came back identically across independent extraction passes; all code quotes are verbatim from files read directly. The repository contains the Piper arm agent server, the SpatialMemory / VLAC / GraspAnything services, and the OpenClaw workspace files and skills; the OpenClaw runtime and the G1 / Go2 clients are not included, so the paper's claims about those parts could not be checked in code. The SpatialMemory offline keyframe pipeline is a placeholder (task_service._simulate_pipeline), the SpatialMemory embeddings are hashed-token and pixel-statistic stand-ins rather than the vision-language encoder described in Sec. 2.3, and no repository code implements the Sec. 2.4 'structured experience' feedback or any mechanism revision.
